data.title: Hi, we're Katie and Michael
data.body:
To those of you who don't know us yet: hi. We're Katie and Michael. We've been best friends for most of our adult lives, and now we're getting married.

We have seen the highest highs and the lowest lows of each other's lives. We both lost our first spouses, too early, to illness. Getting each other through those losses, first one and then the other, brought us closer than either of us would ever have imagined.

Strap in for a Hallmark movie. It's a long and emotional one, but don't worry. It has a happy ending.

data.title: The tiki bar
data.body:
About seventeen years ago, Mike's dad decided to open a tiki bar and crab house in Crisfield, Maryland. Mike worked there over the next few summers, and that's where four people became fast, lifelong friends: Mike, his future wife Bethany, her best friend Katie, and Katie's then-boyfriend Jeremy.

Katie and Jeremy got married first, with Bethany as Maid of Honor. Years later Katie returned the favor at Bethany and Mike's wedding, where Jeremy was the MVP: rebuilding the wilted flower arrangements that morning, hauling bales of hay around, and solving crisis after crisis.

The four of us were thick as thieves.

data.title: The hard years
data.body:
While Mike and Bethany were living in Germany, Bethany became ill and declined very quickly. She was hospitalized in December and passed the following March.

Katie was with Mike on the phone through all of it. Hours at a time, talking about life, pain, love and loss. When he fell down, again and again, she talked him back onto his feet.

Then, in December of 2024, Jeremy was diagnosed with an extremely aggressive cancer. By the following March, he passed in the hospital, surrounded by his loved ones.

Mike knew exactly what Katie was about to go through. This time he was the one on the phone every day, for hours, doing the absolute best he could to support her the way she had supported him.

By then, we had both seen the best and the worst of each other's lives. Bethany and Jeremy are part of this story, and they always will be.

data.title: Water wings
data.body:
Back in Baltimore, Mike was rarely alone but still quite lonely. Eventually he worked up the courage to ask his very best good friend to fit him for some Water Wings and help him jump in the Dating Pool. Katie became his coach.

Bethany had been Mike's first girlfriend, and his best friend before that. He had never really dated, so the plan was to date around for a while.

Then Katie invited him along on her business's yearly weekend cruise, as thanks for getting her through the worst of it, and because it had been years since we'd seen each other in person.

We started dating immediately.

data.title: The elevator
data.body:
By the second day of that cruise, we were standing at the elevator and Mike was mother-fuckering at the universe, because he already knew he wanted to spend the rest of his life with Katie. So much for dating around.

He had never, in his life, felt as at ease, as understood, as seen and loved and accepted as he did in that moment.

And then we started making fart noises.

Katie's son Liam was standing right there with us. He was 10 at the time. Mike has known him his entire life, but he's only now really getting to know him: more resilient than anyone his age should have had to be, still a happy kid despite it, and a world-class smart-ass, which Mike respects.

data.title: Hawaiian shirts, all the time
data.body:
We share a lot of brain chemistry. We think and navigate the world in very similar ways, which is probably why we both say that living together feels like it's always been and brand new at the same time, all the time.

We both carry shared but separate grief, and the love and lessons we earned, painfully, from our first marriages. Whimsy has never been far from either of us, even on the darkest days. At some point we both decided that life had sucked enough to take it too seriously.

Hence Hawaiian shirts. All the time.

Deadpool said it best: her crazy matches his crazy.

You know when you have a sleepover with your best friend as a kid, and something happens (a snowstorm, sufficient pleading, mom and dad's evening out turning into a weekend in Atlantic City) and you find out you get to spend a whole extra night together? That's how Mike describes living with Katie.

We aren't issued a finite ration of love when we clock in to this life. As a really smart lady once put it (paraphrasing): anyone who has had a second kid or a second spouse knows your capacity to love only grows larger as life goes on.

Life is weird. Love is breathtakingly simple.*

*Love may appear differently depending on the user's past experiences, personal traumas, and cultural understanding. User's experience will likely vary. Satisfaction rarely guaranteed.

data.title: The chicken tender prophecy
data.body:
Mike loves chicken tenders. Memes aside. Always has, always will. For decades people told him, 'If you keep eating chicken tenders, you're gonna end up turning into one!'

Years ago, Katie had chickens, until unfortunate events cost her the flock. That fall, Mike moved down to Florida. The coop and run were in disrepair, and Katie had always talked so fondly about her birbs that he got to work rebuilding. By spring we had our first 6 chickens and 8 ducks.

The prophecy was fulfilled. He had become a chicken tender.

Katie worried about Mike moving out here, and honestly so did he. We live in Naples, but not Naples proper, somewhere decidedly more rural than Mike had ever experienced. Turns out he loves it.

We now have like 50 chickens (chicken math be a force of nature, man), 13 of them hatched right here with more on the way, two ducklings named Chorizo and Crunch Wrap Supreme, 6 cats, 1 dog, and a gigantic orb weaver in the chicken coop named Charlotte. Our hearts grow with each new addition.

data.title: The proposal
data.body:
As close to exactly one year later as the universe would allow, we were back on the company cruise.

Mike sucks at planning. He loooooves preparing for things. He loves logistics, details and nuance, and making all the moving parts fit juuuuust right at the last moment. But there are, literally, infinite possibilities for anything. How do you decide? Procrastination and a hurry-up offense, that's how.

Years before, Katie and Jeremy had booked an amazing room for the company cruise, so amazing that Katie booked it again two years in advance. It came with a dedicated butler for our room and like 5 others in this baller-ass section of the VIP section. We were hanging out well above our tax bracket.

It also meant Mike had a co-conspirator on the inside. About 36 hours before we left, he asked Liam how he felt about him asking his mom to marry him. Liam thought hard, rolled his eyes (hard), and said, 'Yeah, that's cool.' Solid.

Mike talked to the room steward, the concierge, the butler, and some dude at the bar named Jeff. (Thanks for the pep talk, sir.) A plan formed. Before dinner, out on the balcony, we would enjoy the view and share a moment. Mike poured a glass of champagne, dropped the ring in the glass, and set Liam to wait five minutes before bringing it out to his mom.

The view was beautiful and blue, the air was warm, and we sat and talked, drowning in our mutual affection. With perfect timing, Liam came out and handed Katie the glass. She smiled, and Mike dropped to his knee.

Mike: 'Will you spend the rest of your life with me?'
Katie: 'Of course. I love you.'
A kiss.
Katie takes a big sip of champagne.
Mike: '…'
Mike: '… shit. She didn't see the ring. She's gonna swallow it.'

Spoiler alert: she said yes, and she didn't drink the ring. It was silly, it was romantic, it was perfect.

The ring is perfect too: vintage 1920s, old mine cut, set in platinum, and, completely by coincidence, exactly 1.37 carats. If you've seen Empire Records, you understand the significance of that number. Katie has '1:37X' tattooed on the inside of her lip. One thirty seven, exactly.

What sort of man can find such a perfect stone in a perfect ring with a perfect story? The kind who lets the lady pick out the ring. Guys, take note.

data.title: Two families
data.body:
Irony abounds: Katie now owns Mike's Plumbing of Southwest Florida. Jeremy's father, Mike Bohall, started the company 30 years ago. About 12 years ago Jeremy took it over, and it has been a family operation ever since. Katie's mom answers the phones, her brother Matt is the most senior tech, and everyone else is family, honorary family, or on the way to being family.

In Florida, there's no such thing as a licensed plumber. A plumber takes a test to become a Plumbing Contractor, and that license doesn't pass down. To keep the doors open, Katie studied constantly through a crash course of 12 weekends, 8 hours a day, Saturday and Sunday, all while raising and homeschooling Liam and running the company. She crushed the contractor's exam.

On the proposal cruise, Katie got to show off the ring to her friends, family and coworkers right away, since most of them were already on the boat. And timing is a funny thing: Matt had been planning to propose to Ashley, his girlfriend of many years, that same weekend. The next evening, with the sun setting, music in the air, and a passed-out drunk guy broiling himself on a nearby lounger, Matt dropped to a knee at the back of the boat. She said yes.

Family is important. You get two families in your life: the one you're born with and the one you choose.

We truly adore each other.
